subtitle: Learn what Executive Order 23-12 sets out about councils and support for agency plans, and how that direction connects to responsible work in your staff role.
scope: For staff learning how Executive Order 23-12, as issued, connects statewide equity direction with agency-specific work. The order is not presented as a detailed staff workforce, purchasing or data checklist. Actual duties, implementation arrangements and required analysis follow the relevant agency policy, plan and authorized process. Practice examples teach those distinctions.
introTranscript: Executive Order 23-12 is titled Providing Equitable, Inclusive, and Effective Government for All. It continues two councils, describes their roles and connects their work to a long-range plan and agency-specific equity plans. It does not supply a complete daily-work checklist for every employee. This course explains what the order actually says, how the councils have different but connected roles, why community perspectives matter and how staff can contribute through their own agency responsibilities. You will practice connecting a practice task to the right source of direction without inventing a council approval requirement or promising a result the evidence does not support. Work at your own pace and use the direct source for the order’s text.

objectives: Describe the order’s purpose and council framework.
Identify a responsibility the text assigns rather than inventing a staff checklist.

lessons.statement: Know which source supplies the direction and which source supplies the actual task.

intro.heading: A statewide framework needs accurate interpretation
intro.body:
Executive Order 23-12 is titled Providing Equitable, Inclusive, and Effective Government for All. Its text describes a commitment to reducing inequities and improving state government. It continues the Governor’s One Minnesota Council on Diversity, Inclusion, and Equity and the Governor’s Community Council on Inclusion and Equity. It also describes support for agency-specific equity plans and the implementation of a long-range plan.

These provisions create a framework for collaboration, advice, plan support and reporting. They are not a complete set of instructions for every employee’s hiring, procurement, data or service task. Those work areas can be relevant to equity, but a lesson should not attribute a detailed checklist to this order when that checklist is not in its text. Agency policies, approved plans and assigned responsibilities provide additional direction for actual work.

Use three distinctions while reading. The executive order states the statewide framework. An agency policy or implementation plan describes the relevant agency requirements and arrangements. A learning example helps you practice applying the ideas. A practice example cannot add a legal duty or grant authority simply because it appears beside the order.

In the practice case for this course, a DHS team reviews how people find a service information session and respond to its invitation. The team wants to connect its work to broader equity direction. It should identify the relevant agency objective and actual responsibility instead of saying the executive order requires every invitation to follow a checklist the team invented. This careful source use makes the connection stronger: the team can explain both why the inquiry matters and how its authorized work addresses it, while preserving what the order does and does not say.

lessons.keyStatement: A learning example may illustrate direction; it cannot rewrite the order.

flashcards.back: A governor’s directive whose actual provisions and authority must be read in context.
The continued bodies and assigned roles described in this order.
The relevant agency plan, policy and authorized arrangements for carrying out work.
A practice situation that illustrates an idea without creating a new legal duty.

items.title: Purpose
items.body: The title and rationale connect equity, inclusion and effectiveness. Do not reduce the order to a claim that every change has already produced an equitable result. The text provides direction and roles, while evidence is needed to understand implementation and effects.

items.title: Text
items.body: Locate a provision before attributing a requirement to it. The order includes councils, agency-plan support and reporting. It does not specify every field in a staff worksheet or every step in procurement. A useful summary identifies that limit clearly.

items.title: Actual work
items.body: Find the relevant agency requirement and assigned responsibility for the task. At DHS, the Equity Policy provides separate equity-lens and analysis expectations. This course’s invitation example helps practice source distinctions; it is not the required analysis itself.

tabs.label: Accurate order summary
tabs.body: The order continues two councils and describes their roles in equitable state practices and plan implementation. This gives a useful overview without inventing a daily operating manual.

tabs.label: Agency responsibility
tabs.body: The team uses the applicable DHS policy and business-area implementation arrangements for its invitation review. The connection is practical, but the source of the actual responsibility should be identified accurately.

tabs.label: Invented checklist
tabs.body: Saying EO 23-12 requires these twelve purchasing and data fields misattributes a learning worksheet or separate procedure to the order. Use the appropriate source for those fields and do not present them as the order’s text.

check.question: Which summary stays within the order’s text?
check.correct: It continues two councils and describes plan support, collaboration, advice and reporting roles.
wrong: It contains every step for each DHS purchasing decision.
It automatically authorizes every staff member to change program rules.
It guarantees that every state action has equitable results.
check.feedbackCorrect: This describes the framework the order actually establishes without adding a staff checklist or outcome guarantee.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The order does not supply universal task authority, a detailed manual for every business area or proof of outcomes. Read its provisions and use the relevant agency sources for actual implementation.

sorting.heading: Order provision, agency procedure or learning example?

items.text: Continue the two councils described in the text.
Assign council reporting on the long-range plan.
Use the applicable agency release process for a real invitation.
Follow the DHS Equity Policy for an actual covered action.
Practice reviewing a practice invitation.
Compare practice wording options in this course.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A summary calls a newly invented staff data checklist a direct requirement of EO 23-12.
options: Describe the order’s actual framework and identify the proper source, if any, for the staff checklist.
Keep the attribution because the checklist sounds useful.
Assume the order contains every detail not found in agency policy.
responses: This preserves useful practice while making its authority and source accurate.
Usefulness does not make a statement part of the order.
Missing details should not be invented and attributed to the executive order.

lessons.transfer: Write one accurate sentence about the order and one about a separate agency responsibility.

move.control: You can explain the framework without inventing staff obligations.
move.failure: A useful idea is incorrectly presented as the order’s requirement.
move.next: Compare the practice claim with the direct order text.

lessons.title: Understand the two councils’ connected roles
lessons.summary: Distinguish collaboration and monitoring from community advice and representation.
lessons.objective: Describe the One Minnesota Council’s collaboration and monitoring roles.
objectives: Describe the One Minnesota Council’s collaboration and monitoring roles.
Describe the Community Council’s advisory role.
Explain why the order does not create a universal council approval step for staff work.
takeaways: The two councils have connected but different roles.
The Community Council contributes advice and community perspectives.
Advice and monitoring are not a universal approval or veto process.
lessons.statement: Keep the assigned role clear when describing a council’s influence.

image.caption: Colleagues listen to one another around a conference table with laptops and notes.

intro.heading: Connected roles do not mean identical responsibilities
intro.body:
The order continues the Governor’s One Minnesota Council on Diversity, Inclusion, and Equity. Its text describes a space where equity practitioners and agency leaders collaborate on effective, inclusive and equitable practices. It assigns monitoring and advice concerning implementation of legislative policies and state programs aimed at reducing inequities and institutional barriers. The order also connects its work with the full Governor’s Cabinet and collaboration with the Community Council.

The Community Council has a related advisory role. The order describes members appointed by the Governor, with sought representation from communities affected by disparities, inequities and systemic racism. It provides for advice and collaboration with the One Minnesota Council, specified governor’s offices, state agencies and agency equity practitioners. It also assigns the Community Council review of the One Minnesota Council’s annual report.

These roles should not be changed into an approval or veto requirement for every employee task. The order’s advisory language matters. In this example, a team can use its own authorized engagement and implementation process without claiming that a council has approved the invitation or must sign every draft. Advice can influence the work while decision responsibilities remain in their appropriate settings.

The order also specifies membership and administrative support arrangements. Those provisions show how the framework is organized, but this course does not identify current officeholders or claim that a particular meeting or consultation has occurred. When actual work needs a current route, confirm it through the responsible agency process. The learning goal is to understand what the order assigns and how the roles connect, not to create a new contact directory or a permission gate for ordinary staff contributions.

lessons.keyStatement: Council influence should be described with the advisory and implementation roles the text actually assigns.

flashcards.back: The continued council with collaboration, monitoring, advice and annual reporting roles described in the order.
The continued council with advisory, collaboration and annual-report review roles described in the order.
A role providing advice and perspectives, rather than a universal authority to approve every task.
The facilitation, staffing and support arrangements the order assigns to the specified offices.

items.title: Collaboration
items.body: The One Minnesota Council’s work brings practitioners and leaders together and involves the Cabinet. Collaboration can help connect agency efforts, but the course should not claim that collaboration automatically resolves every barrier or replaces agency responsibilities.

items.title: Community perspective
items.body: The Community Council’s membership and advisory role are intended to bring affected community perspectives into statewide work. Council membership does not establish that every person or every relevant experience has been represented in an individual agency decision.

items.title: Authority
items.body: A team should not invent council approval as a new prerequisite for its routine work. Identify actual decision authority and any required consultation from the applicable source. An advisory role is meaningful without being described as a blanket veto.

tabs.heading: How the roles may be described

tabs.label: Monitoring and advice
tabs.body: The order assigns the One Minnesota Council monitoring and advice on relevant policy and program implementation. Describe this role accurately rather than treating it as a claim that the council personally performs every agency task.

tabs.label: Advice and collaboration
tabs.body: The Community Council advises the specified offices, agencies and practitioners and collaborates with the One Minnesota Council. Its input can inform choices; it should not be claimed as unanimous agreement from every affected community.

tabs.label: Invented sign-off
tabs.body: A practice invitation is not council-approved simply because a course discusses the council framework. Staff should not add an unsupported sign-off label or imply current consultation that has not actually occurred.

check.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the roles?
check.correct: The Community Council acts in an advisory capacity, and the One Minnesota Council has the text’s collaboration, monitoring and reporting roles.
wrong: Every staff document needs both councils’ signatures.
The Community Council can be described as every affected person’s unanimous agreement.
A lesson mentioning a council proves that council reviewed the team’s work.
check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps the roles and influence connected without inventing approval or representation claims.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The order does not create a universal signature requirement or show that a practice task was reviewed. Community advice is valuable, but it is not evidence of unanimous agreement or every individual experience.

sorting.heading: One Minnesota role, Community Council role or unsupported claim?

items.text: Monitor and advise on relevant policy and program implementation.
Prepare the assigned annual long-range-plan report.
Act in an advisory capacity to the specified offices, agencies and practitioners.
Review the One Minnesota Council’s annual report.
Approve every employee invitation draft.
Represent unanimous agreement from all affected people.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A team wants to label its invitation council-approved after reading this course. Neither council reviewed it.
options: Remove the unsupported label and identify the actual agency review that applies.
Keep the label to demonstrate commitment.
Ask classmates to stand in for both councils and approve it.
responses: This preserves accurate authority and avoids implying a review that did not occur.
A positive intention does not make an approval claim true.
A class activity cannot impersonate the councils or their assigned roles.

lessons.transfer: Describe each council’s role and one approval claim the text does not establish.

move.control: You can explain meaningful advice without inventing a permission gate.
move.failure: A council label substitutes for actual review or authority.
move.next: Use the direct text to distinguish the practice approval claim.

lessons.title: Connect agency plans to a concrete staff contribution
lessons.summary: Link a task to the relevant agency objective without replacing required analysis.
lessons.objective: Explain the order’s support for agency-specific equity plans.

Connect a practice task to an appropriate agency objective and responsibility.
Distinguish a practice note from required DHS analysis.

Staff contributions should identify their actual objective and responsibility.
A connection to a plan does not certify the work or complete required analysis.
lessons.statement: Show how the task contributes and which agency process governs it.

image.caption: Colleagues listen to one another around a conference table with laptops and notes.

intro.heading: A plan connection should be more than a label
intro.body:
The order says the Office of Inclusion will work with state agency equity and inclusion practitioners to support progress on agency-specific equity plans and implementation of the long-range plan. This connects statewide direction with agency work. It does not write every agency objective, assign every staff task or turn each course exercise into an official implementation step. The relevant agency plan and authorized responsibilities still need to be identified.

For DHS, the Equity Policy supplies separate expectations about using an equity lens in daily work and agency actions. It identifies toolkit uses across policy, budgets, service delivery, employment and other areas. It also requires formal analysis for covered prolonged or long-term actions scheduled for leadership approval, using the specified analysis or scan or a customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director. These are agency-policy provisions, not a detailed checklist found in EO 23-12.

In the practice invitation review, staff can connect the task to an agency objective concerning usable service information, if that is the applicable plan direction. They should identify the actual objective rather than invent its official wording. A practical contribution describes the missing instruction, relevant perspectives, possible options and next decision responsibility. The connection is credible because the task and process are explained, not merely because the note contains the word equity.

The One DSD consultant can help staff frame questions and develop their capability. That support should not be misrepresented as the equity-director role in the policy’s customized-tool condition or as universal consultant approval for every staff task. Keep the relevant source and responsibility clear. This course’s practice connection is preparation; actual plan implementation and required analysis continue through the authorized agency arrangements.

inThisLesson: Preserve required analysis and role distinctions.
lessons.keyStatement: A task-plan connection is useful when its purpose, evidence and responsibility are visible.

flashcards.back: The relevant agency direction supported by the order’s plan provisions.
An explanation of how a concrete contribution relates to an applicable objective.
The specified agency-policy process for covered actions, distinct from this learning note.
Accurate separation of consultant support, equity-director policy roles and assigned decision authority.

items.title: Objective
items.body: Use the actual plan wording or confirm the relevant direction through the authorized process. A course can illustrate an access objective, but it cannot invent an official agency commitment or claim that an unverified label is current plan text.

items.title: Contribution
items.body: The practice team can describe the response instruction, an evidence question and a proposed review. This shows what the task may contribute. It is stronger than placing a goal number beside the invitation without explaining the actual work.

items.title: Required process
items.body: A learning note does not replace the DHS Equity Analysis or Scan required for a covered action. The policy’s role and tool conditions remain. Optional consultant support may help preparation while staff and the people or areas responsible carry out their assigned work.

tabs.label: Direction only
tabs.body: A general statement that equity matters can explain intent but leaves the task unclear. Name the applicable objective and actual work so the reader can see what is being proposed and which responsibility follows.

tabs.label: Concrete contribution
tabs.body: The note connects a supported instruction concern to a relevant access objective and names the responsible review. It states uncertainty and does not claim a completed outcome before evidence exists.

tabs.label: Automatic compliance
tabs.body: Matching a task to a plan label does not prove legal compliance, equitable results or completion of the required analysis. The formal process and evidence cannot be replaced by a heading or a course answer.

check.question: What makes the practice task-plan connection useful?
check.correct: Identify the applicable agency objective, actual contribution, evidence limit and responsible process.
wrong: Add a goal label and declare every requirement complete.
Call the course note the customized policy tool without the required equity-director consultation.
Require consultant approval for every routine task regardless of the actual procedure.
check.feedbackCorrect: This explains the contribution and preserves the roles and requirements that apply.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A label cannot establish compliance or tool authorization. The policy’s customized-tool condition and actual procedures remain distinct from consultant guidance and classroom practice.

sorting.heading: Plan connection, required agency process or overclaim?

items.text: Explain how the practice instruction review relates to the applicable access objective.
Describe the task and evidence question beside the objective.
Use the specified DHS analysis process for an actual covered action.
Preserve the equity-director consultation condition for a customized tool.
A goal label proves every policy requirement is complete.
The course itself authorizes a new official agency objective.

lessons.next: Next, consider how affected perspectives can inform the actual work.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A team adds an agency goal heading to an invitation review and calls formal analysis complete.
options: Explain the concrete contribution and preserve any actual analysis requirement and role conditions.
Treat the heading as the required analysis.
Assume every routine draft must receive council and consultant approval.
responses: This makes the connection useful without replacing the applicable process.
A heading cannot complete the required analysis.
The course and order do not create universal approval gates.

lessons.transfer: Map a practice task to an illustrative objective, a contribution and the actual responsibility that would need confirmation.

move.control: You can connect your work to direction without inventing authority or completion.
move.failure: A plan label replaces meaningful action or the required process.
move.next: Practice with the practice task and keep actual plan wording within its proper source.

lessons.title: Bring affected perspectives into a real open choice
lessons.summary: Apply the order’s community emphasis without overstating representation or influence.
lessons.objective: Describe how the order connects community perspectives to statewide work.
objectives: Describe how the order connects community perspectives to statewide work.
Identify a meaningful question and open choice in the practice case.
Explain input’s influence accurately without claiming universal representation.
takeaways: The order connects community advice with state practices and plan work.
Participation needs a purpose and an accurate account of influence.
A council or meeting does not automatically represent every affected experience.
lessons.statement: Make participation relevant to a choice that can still be informed.

image.caption: Colleagues listen to one another around a conference table with laptops and notes.

intro.heading: Community emphasis needs practical follow-through
intro.body:
The order’s rationale emphasizes involving people affected by state decisions. Its provisions connect the One Minnesota Council with the Community Council and describe sought representation and community advice. This is a meaningful part of the framework. It should not be reduced to a claim that listing a council or holding a meeting automatically gives every affected person a voice in a particular decision.

In the practice invitation review, the team can ask how people find and use the response routes. That is a relevant task question. The team should identify which choice is still open, what is outside the review and how input will be considered. It should not invite people to redesign eligibility if the team only has responsibility for accurate instructions. Use the actual authorized engagement process for real work and be truthful about its limits.

Different perspectives may illuminate different steps. People using the invitation may describe a term that was unfamiliar, while staff can explain the requirement behind it. One participant cannot be required to speak for an entire community. Avoid unnecessary identity or personal disclosures and consider suitable communication and participation support through applicable arrangements. Do not promise confidentiality or a service change beyond the process’s authority.

After input is reviewed, explain how it informed the decision. It may support clearer wording, identify another inquiry or support an unchanged requirement with reasons. Meaningful participation does not require every preference to be adopted. It does require an honest account of influence rather than pretending a closed decision is open. This course uses a practice task to practice those habits; it does not create a substitute Community Council or establish that actual engagement requirements have been met.

inThisLesson: Explain how input informed the decision.
lessons.keyStatement: Represent the process’s influence and limits accurately.

flashcards.back: Knowledge from someone whose experience may be shaped by the decision.
A decision that can still be informed by relevant evidence or input.
The boundary of what one person, group or meeting can establish about others’ experiences.
An explanation of how input was considered, including reasons for unchanged choices.

accordion.heading: Make the invitation to contribute useful

items.title: Purpose
items.body: Explain that the practice review concerns finding and using response routes. This gives people a practical question and avoids collecting unrelated personal histories. If input reveals a broader relevant concern, identify a proper next process rather than promising an immediate change.

items.title: Influence
items.body: Say which instruction choices are open and which requirements are outside the team’s authority. Do not describe participation as control over every decision. Accurate limits respect people’s time and allow them to decide what contribution is worthwhile.

items.title: Follow-through
items.body: Explain how the input informed the reviewed choice, including an unchanged requirement and its reason. Attendance is not evidence of universal agreement. A report should reflect what actually happened and where relevant perspectives or information remain missing.

tabs.label: Token example
tabs.body: One participant is asked to speak for every person with a similar background. This can misstate the knowledge supplied and hide variation. Invite the person’s own experience and identify further relevant perspectives without forcing disclosure.

tabs.label: Focused inquiry
tabs.body: A clear task question and open choice help people contribute usable knowledge. Compare that input with the actual requirement and implementation information. Neither experience nor staff knowledge alone must be treated as the entire account.

tabs.label: Closed choice
tabs.body: If the decision is already final, do not say all choices are open. A later feedback process may examine implementation or future review, but its purpose should be described accurately instead of presenting it as influence over a closed choice.

check.question: Which statement accurately describes the practice participation process?
check.correct: Explain the response-route question, what is open and how input will be considered and followed through.
wrong: Attendance means everyone in the community agreed.
One person is responsible for explaining all experiences of their group.
A final choice is still open because the team wants more favorable feedback.
check.feedbackCorrect: This connects relevant knowledge to a truthful process and real opportunity to inform the work.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Attendance and a single perspective cannot establish universal agreement or representation. Participation should not pretend a closed choice is open, and it should not impose group-spokesperson duties on an individual.

sorting.heading: Relevant inquiry, accurate influence or misleading claim?

items.text: Ask how people find the response instruction.
Seek appropriate perspectives about using the route.
Explain which communication choice remains open.
Explain why input supported an unchanged requirement.
Attendance proves universal community agreement.
The course team is now the Governor’s Community Council.

lessons.next: Next, understand reporting and monitoring without confusing activity with results.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: Feedback supports clearer instructions but the eligibility requirement remains unchanged.
options: How the feedback informed the instruction and why the requirement remains, with any appropriate next inquiry.
That no input mattered because one requirement did not change.
That participants approved every agency decision.
responses: This describes real influence and reasons without claiming universal approval.
Input can inform implementation and the reasoning for an unchanged choice.
Feedback about one task does not supply approval for every decision.

lessons.transfer: Write a practice participation question, an influence limit and a follow-through statement.

move.control: You can use the community emphasis without exaggerating representation.
move.failure: A meeting becomes a claim that every voice or requirement was satisfied.
move.next: Practice the practice open choice and explain its limits.

lessons.title: Understand what reporting and monitoring can show
lessons.summary: Separate council report responsibilities, staff evidence and outcome claims.
lessons.objective: Identify the annual report responsibility assigned by the order.
objectives: Identify the annual report responsibility assigned by the order.
Distinguish activity evidence from evidence about results.
State a review limit without treating missing information as reassurance.
takeaways: The annual report is a specified council responsibility.
Task completion and intended results are different questions.
Unknown information should remain unknown until suitable evidence supports a conclusion.
lessons.statement: Report what the evidence supports and who holds the actual reporting responsibility.

image.caption: Colleagues listen to one another around a conference table with laptops and notes.

intro.heading: A report should show progress without inventing certainty
intro.body:
The order assigns the One Minnesota Council an annual report to the Governor on the status and implementation of the long-range plan, beginning in 2024, with submission by December 31. It assigns the Community Council review of that report. These are council responsibilities in the text. The course should not tell every employee that the order requires them to submit their own report to the Governor by that date. Any staff reporting duty must come from the actual agency arrangement that applies to their work.

Staff may contribute evidence through assigned agency processes. A useful contribution identifies the task, what was done, what the information measures and what remains uncertain. In the practice invitation case, a released revision is evidence that an implementation step occurred. It does not establish that everyone understood the invitation, had usable access or received the intended service benefit. An appropriate review needs information relevant to those result questions.

Check the comparison before drawing conclusions. Response totals from different periods, different definitions or different opportunities may not provide a suitable comparison. A later change does not establish that the invitation alone caused the result. Keep actual information use and disclosure within applicable protections, particularly when small groups or individual circumstances could be identified.

Monitoring can identify progress, unresolved conditions and questions for further review. It should not turn a blank record into no warning signs or invent a favorable figure to make a report look complete. Say which information is missing and what responsible next step could clarify it. This learning activity develops careful reporting habits without certifying the council’s present implementation or requiring learners to gather actual protected records.

lessons.keyStatement: An implementation record is useful evidence, but it is not proof of every intended outcome.

flashcards.back: The annual long-range-plan reporting responsibility assigned to the One Minnesota Council.
Information showing whether and how an action was carried out.
Information relevant to what the action helped people do or experience.
A matter not established by the information available, rather than an automatic positive or negative result.

accordion.heading: Prepare evidence for the relevant review

items.title: Assigned responsibility
items.body: Know where your actual contribution belongs and who holds the reporting role. A council deadline in the order does not automatically create the same deadline and recipient for every employee. Use the authorized agency arrangement rather than inventing one.

items.title: What the measure shows
items.body: A count of invitations released describes activity. A suitable question about finding and using the response route examines a different result. Explain the measure’s scope instead of treating the easiest available count as the full outcome.

items.title: A missing figure
items.body: If no suitable result information is available, say so. The gap can inform the next inquiry, but it cannot be labeled success, failure or a proven cause. Missing records should not be replaced with made-up zeros or reassuring statements.

tabs.label: Supported progress
tabs.body: The reviewed invitation was released is supported by the practice implementation record. The report can acknowledge this step while keeping the route-use question open.

tabs.label: Unsupported result
tabs.body: Everyone’s access improved is stronger than the release record supports. A suitable review may show useful effects and remaining barriers, but the record alone cannot establish a universal outcome.

tabs.label: Transparent gap
tabs.body: “We do not yet have comparable information about use” identifies the limit and helps plan a responsible next step. It is more informative than no concerns exist simply because a field is blank.

check.question: What should a practice report say when the revised invitation was released but its use has not been reviewed?
check.correct: The revision was implemented; relevant results remain to be examined through appropriate evidence.
wrong: Everyone benefited because the invitation changed.
The blank result field proves there are no barriers.
EO 23-12 requires every employee to send a separate report directly to the Governor.
check.feedbackCorrect: This records progress at the level supported and preserves the relevant reporting roles.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Task completion does not establish universal benefit, and missing evidence is not reassurance. The order’s council report responsibility should not be reassigned to every employee by a learning example.

sorting.heading: Council responsibility, supported evidence or unsupported conclusion?

items.text: The One Minnesota Council prepares the assigned annual report.
The Community Council reviews that annual report.
The practice release record shows the invitation revision occurred.
A note identifies that comparable route-use information is still missing.
A blank figure means every barrier is resolved.
Every learner must submit an annual report to the Governor under this order.

lessons.next: Next, combine accurate sources, a concrete contribution and responsible follow-through.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A progress table has no route-use figures and labels the quarter no access concerns.
options: State that route-use results are unknown and identify a suitable next evidence question.
Keep the reassuring label because missing figures cannot show a problem.
Replace the blank field with an invented positive number.
responses: This reports the information limit honestly and supports the next inquiry.
Missing evidence cannot establish that no concerns exist.
A fabricated figure undermines the report and the decision it informs.

lessons.transfer: Write one supported practice progress statement and one honest evidence limit.

move.control: You can distinguish reporting roles and claim only what the evidence supports.
move.failure: A completed action or blank field becomes a universal success claim.
move.next: Review the practice implementation record and state the result question that remains.

Explain the learning exercise’s limits and a suitable review question.
takeaways: The order’s direction should connect to actual work through the appropriate sources.
A supported staff contribution needs evidence and responsibility.
Learning completion does not prove plan implementation or full compliance.
lessons.statement: Make the connection clear enough to guide the next responsible action.

intro.heading: Connect the direction to your daily work
intro.body:
The order matters to staff when its statewide direction connects to an actual task and the appropriate agency responsibility. A short note can make that connection without repeating the entire council structure or introducing technical language into routine communication. Identify why the inquiry matters, what the team is examining, which source governs the actual work and what should happen next.

For the practice invitation, the note might connect usable service information to the relevant agency objective, describe the missing response instruction and propose review of a supported wording option. It should identify the responsible release role and any unresolved access or resource question. It should not say the councils approved the task, the executive order supplies every procedural step or the consultant has performed the staff work. Those statements would misrepresent authority or responsibility.

Optional consultant support can help staff improve the question, evidence and interpretation. Staff can still develop their own work and use resources across DHS. Required agency analysis, reporting and approval responsibilities remain with the actual roles and procedures. A practice note does not become an official equity plan, create a customized-tool authorization or complete required training simply because it was written in this course.

Include follow-through that fits the task. Describe what was reviewed, how relevant input informed the decision and what evidence would help examine the result. An unchanged choice can be explained with reasons; it need not be altered just to demonstrate course completion. Use practice material or a suitable draft at your own pace. The course builds source awareness and practical capability, while actual operating work continues through the authorized agency arrangements.

lessons.keyStatement: A clear connection supports responsible work; it does not create authority or certify results.

flashcards.back: A concise explanation linking the broader purpose to a specific contribution.
The actual policy, plan or authorized arrangement governing the next action.
The assigned role for carrying out or deciding the next step.
A suitable question about implementation or results, with evidence limits stated.

items.title: Clear wording
items.body: Explain the invitation concern in ordinary language. A reader should see the task and reason without needing a council acronym on every line. Keep the source distinction available where it supports the actual responsibility.

items.title: Responsible next step
items.body: Propose review by the appropriate role and identify the conditions that remain. Do not promise resources, eligibility changes or a release outside your authority. A useful recommendation can be specific without becoming an unauthorized commitment.

items.title: Learning boundary
items.body: A completed exercise can show what the learner practiced. It cannot certify the council’s current work or replace the agency’s required analysis. Keep the actual operating requirement distinct from the learning record.

tabs.label: Practical connection
tabs.body: The practice note names the task, an applicable agency objective, evidence and the next responsible review. It makes the statewide connection visible through actual work rather than a decorative label.

tabs.label: Authority drift
tabs.body: A note claiming council approval or an invented executive-order checklist creates a false picture of the process. Remove the unsupported claim and use the source that actually supplies the responsibility.

tabs.label: Outcome certainty
tabs.body: A note promising that one revision will eliminate every inequity goes beyond the evidence. State what the option addresses and what the next review can examine. Honest limits do not make the contribution unimportant.

check.question: Which final note is most useful?
check.correct: Connect the practice task to appropriate direction, state evidence and limits, and identify the responsible next process.
wrong: Claim both councils approved the task because the learner studied them.
Certify all plan outcomes from course completion.
Present consultant feedback as a substitute for required agency analysis.
check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps the connection concrete, accurate and ready for a responsible next action.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Studying a council does not establish its approval, and course completion or consultant feedback cannot certify actual outcomes or replace formal requirements. Use the appropriate source, evidence and assigned responsibility.

sorting.heading: Useful contribution, formal responsibility or unsupported claim?

items.text: Describe the practice instruction concern and supported option.
State the evidence limit and result question.
Use the actual agency analysis process for a covered action.
Keep release decisions with the authorized role.
The councils approved the invitation because their names appear in the course.
Course completion proves every agency plan goal is achieved.

lessons.next: Use the job aid to practice an accurate connection at your own pace.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: Your note accurately identifies an instruction concern but adds council-approved and full compliance without evidence.
options: Remove the unsupported claims and preserve the task, evidence and responsible next review.
Keep the claims because they make the note sound official.
Discard the entire inquiry because it cannot certify every outcome.
responses: This retains the useful contribution and repairs the authority and evidence claims.
Official-sounding language cannot supply a review or result that did not occur.
A bounded inquiry remains useful without a universal certificate.

lessons.transfer: Prepare a practice note identifying direction, task, evidence, responsible next process and review limit.

move.control: You can connect the order’s framework to practical staff work accurately.
move.failure: A framework label becomes an invented approval, mandate or outcome guarantee.
move.next: Practice with the practice case or a suitable draft without disclosing actual protected records.

jobAid.subtitle: From statewide direction to a responsible contribution
remember: EO 23-12 provides councils, roles and plan support. Use the relevant agency policy and authorized arrangements for actual tasks; this learning note does not create new duties or certify outcomes.

sections.heading: Read the order accurately
items: It continues the One Minnesota Council and the Community Council with connected but distinct roles.
The Community Council’s advisory role is not a universal staff approval or veto process.
The order supports agency-specific equity plans rather than supplying every task checklist.

sections.heading: Find the actual agency responsibility
items: Identify the relevant objective and proper source; do not invent official plan wording.
Use DHS Equity Policy requirements and assigned roles for actual covered analysis.
Consultant guidance can support staff capability without becoming a universal permission gate or replacing an equity-director policy role.

sections.heading: Make participation useful
items: Identify a relevant question and a choice that can still be informed.
State influence and information limits honestly; one person does not represent everyone.
Explain how input informed the choice, including unchanged decisions and reasons.

sections.heading: Report at the strength supported
items: The order assigns annual reporting to the One Minnesota Council and report review to the Community Council.
Staff evidence and deadlines follow the actual agency process, not an invented direct report to the Governor.
Separate action from result, and state missing information as unknown.

sections.heading: Prepare the next contribution
items: Name the task, evidence, proposed action and responsible next review.
Do not claim council approval, resources or outcomes that have not been established.
Learning practice does not establish full compliance or actual plan completion.

sources.title: Executive Order 23-12 — Equitable, Inclusive, and Effective Government
sources.note: The direct four-page order continues two councils, describes their roles, supports agency-specific equity plans and sets council reporting responsibilities. It does not contain a detailed checklist for every staff task.

sources.title: DHS — Equity Policy
sources.note: Separate agency expectations for equity-lens work, employee and leadership roles, toolkit use and required formal analysis. Learning about the executive order does not replace these responsibilities.
